title: The Effect of Calorie Posting Regulation on Consumer Opinion: A Flexible Latent Dirichlet Allocation Model with Informative Priors
authors: Dinesh Puranam; Vishal Narayan; Vrinda Kadiyali
eligible_reason: Not staggered and not eligible as estimated. NYC calorie-posting regulation takes effect at a single common date (Post = July 2008 onward for all restaurants); DiD compares chain (treated) vs. non-chain restaurants' review topic proportions. Estimated by lmer with REML random intercepts for restaurant and author plus zip FE (random effects in place of unit FE: 5b ruling), in +/-6/12/24-month windows and alternative Post dates.
design_notes: main_result.r: lmer(topic_0*1000 ~ chain_flag*Post + addressZip + (1|name) + (1|author_id), REML=TRUE). Topic proportions come from the authors' LDA (Java) MCMC snapshot (Output/calories_snapshot.csv).
data_files_note: Processed review text, metadata and an LDA MCMC snapshot with topic proportions are shipped.
data_provenance_note: Real Yelp-type reviews processed into topic proportions by the authors' LDA model; outcome is a model output (MCMC snapshot).
software_notes: Java (LDA model), R (lme4) for the DiD, Python for author analysis.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available; screened from README, code and OpenAlex abstract (which describes a DiD around the 2008 NYC regulation). Single treatment date, so ineligible regardless of the REML issue.
